findings.title: Final provider validation can become stale during subsequent awaited checks
findings.rationale: After the claim transaction releases its locks, OutboundService.finalProviderFence awaits contextBeforeDispatch, then policy.inspect, then the actor callback. The callback locks only user, grant and BU rows; its final checks cover the signed session and captured deadlines. A credential replacement or generation-changing disconnect committed after the provider-context observation can therefore escape this common fence while the actor remains authorized and the operation retains its previously decrypted credential. The Channel contract provides no guarantee of another provider-tuple observation after these awaits. The native authorization tests hold this same context-read boundary but mutate only grants/session; accepted-fact tests mutate credentials after POST. This is an uncovered source-supported interleaving, not a demonstrated production failure. It conflicts with IG-ARCH-R1-01's requirement to validate the captured current tuple before external dispatch.
findings.suggested_action: Make the final local observation coherently validate the captured provider, generation, credential, readiness and actor facts at the last awaited boundary, followed by synchronous session/deadline checks. Preserve abstract policy ownership, short transactions and HTTP outside transactions. Add native held-boundary cases for actual reauthorization and disconnect with a live actor, requiring zero message POSTs and matched unchanged-context controls.
